inputs.text: They want us to believe Mary Ngechi Ngethe was the whole story: unsuitable cemetery land bought for Ksh.283 million, then the money supposedly recovered from her. That neat ending is exactly what should raise questions. Pinning everything on one committee chair can close the case in public while leaving the wider procurement process—and whoever benefited from it—out of sight. “Recovered” money doesn’t prove the system was clean; it may just make the cover story look complete.

output.main_topic: Skepticism that the Mary Ngechi Ngethe account and recovered cemetery-land money obscure wider procurement accountability
subtopics: Alleged recovery of money from Mary Ngechi Ngethe
Possible scapegoating and concealment of procurement beneficiaries

output.narrative_frame: Skeptical framing suggests that blaming one committee chair and highlighting recovered money could conceal wider procurement accountability.
opinions: The neat ending should raise questions.
